Users are named only loosely (agencies, possibly university), with no clear operator/customer distinction and funding is speculative. Referencing is partly from weak sources and Wikipedia is used despite the explicit prohibition."},{"id":"C2","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Orbit","quote":"the satellite will be positioned at an altitude of 600km above Earth’s surface"},{"where":"Orbit","quote":"Ω 27.33° The initial value indicates the location of the launch facility."},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","quote":"Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory"}],"reasoning":"Orbit and STK access results are presented with a COE table and screenshots. However, the launch section is inconsistent (Vega VV18 vs Vega E from Kourou, while also claiming a 2025 launch), the RAAN value is unjustified and not tied to the launch site, the orbit is described as retrograde yet the RAAN/launch logic is confused, and the Mount Pleasant ground station is a radio observatory, not a practical operator facility. EOL is unfinished (truncated drag-sail text), and 5.05°N latitude for Kourou is roughly correct but the 'larger than inclination' window argument is wrong. Software files not evidenced."},{"id":"C3","level":"Deficient","mark":2,"evidence":[{"where":"Conclusion","quote":"A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet."}],"reasoning":"Conclusion mainly restates the design with generic claims; it does not draw evidence-based conclusions about performance, limitations, or EOL outcomes, and it introduces unsupported statements about preventing bleaching."},{"id":"C4","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","quote":"The most promising alternative is a ‘drag sail’ – a drag-enhancing deorbit device that deploys at the EOL. It acts like a regular sail, utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable"},{"where":"Bibliography","quote":"[6] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_in_spaceflight. [Online]."}],"reasoning":"Structure follows requested headings with figures captioned, but there are truncated sentences, a broken table, mislabelled figure references, inconsistent numbering of access tables, and unformatted citations. R4 met but inconsistent; R5 met; R6 partly; R7 met; R8 partly (EOL unfinished); R9 partly; R10 partly (screenshots, no software files evidenced); R11 partly (Wikipedia use)."}],"requirements":[{"id":"R1","met":"yes","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R2","met":"yes","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R3","met":"partial","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R4","met":"partial","where":"Launch"},{"id":"R5","met":"yes","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R6","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R7","met":"yes","where":"Ground Control & Communications"},{"id":"R8","met":"partial","where":"Mission Duration & EOL"},{"id":"R9","met":"partial","where":"Ground Control & Communications"},{"id":"R10","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R11","met":"no","where":"Bibliography"}],"technical_issues":[{"where":"Launch","issue":"Vega VV18 is said to be the rideshare option but the design then selects Vega E from Kourou, which is not yet built, creating inconsistency with the claimed 2025 launch."},{"where":"Launch","issue":"Claims the launch window count depends on latitude being smaller than inclination; the reasoning is confused and does not justify the choice."},{"where":"Orbit","issue":"RAAN of 27.33° is stated as the launch facility location, but RAAN is not set by the site alone; no justification from launch time or sun-synchronous node drift is given."},{"where":"Orbit","issue":"Says a sun-synchronous orbit requires RAAN to change 360° per year, yet also that the orbit is retrograde while describing 'near-polar' without giving the sun-synchronous rate calculation."},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","issue":"Stated that polar ground stations maximise pass frequency; the Tasmanian site is not polar and the choice is justified against the stated logic."},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","issue":"Claims uncontrolled descent requires least energy but then the drag sail is proposed without any deorbit time or altitude analysis."}],"overall":"The report covers the required segments with STK outputs but has significant technical inconsistencies in launch and orbit logic, an unfinished EOL section, a weak conclusion, and presentation/citation errors including a prohibited Wikipedia source. Overall a mid-to-low adequate submission."}
